WHY_A_NEW_PROBE_WAS_UNAVOIDABLE_ring_IS_.finding: The brief told me to run `probes.py ring` on r5 and r6 05-cut+500ms. I did — 3.354 (mask 3763) -> 3.619 (mask 5031) — and then I RENDERED THE MASK, and it does not touch the pith collar at any angle. `ring`'s band is the annulus between the 0.55 and 0.7425 scaled second-moment ellipses of the largest luma component OF THE WHOLE FRAME, which on 05-cut+500ms is BOTH melon halves plus the rind plus the juice bridging them. On shots/r5 the band renders as two horizontal stripes lying across the far half's flesh and the near half's lower rind; on shots/r6 it is a broad C over rind and background. It is a whole-body shading statistic wearing the collar's name.
WHY_A_NEW_PROBE_WAS_UNAVOIDABLE_ring_IS_.and_it_is_not_even_comparable_across_the: Because the band is keyed to a whole-frame ellipse, a pose change resizes it. r5 -> r6 the fitted ellipse went a=61.7/b=55.9 to a=60.6/b=38.9 and mask_px 3763 -> 5031 — a 34% different region. 3.354 vs 3.619 is not two readings of the same set of surfaces. The same caveat applies to `clip:05`, whose mask moved 9490 -> 6858 px between the two rounds.
WHY_A_NEW_PROBE_WAS_UNAVOIDABLE_ring_IS_.also_correcting_the_brief: The brief says 'r5 collar had 12-sector max/min of 1.35 where the reference measures ~3.9'. 3.9 is not a reference number — 3.95 is what the r4 RENDER measured on the r5 critic's own band. The reference numbers in that verdict are 2.77 (plate-02 lemon silhouette peel annulus) and, on plate-01's pith, 'FLAT across the ~100 deg of arc that is visible'. Through my `collar` probe plate-01 reads 1.257. We have been chasing a target that was our own previous frame.
WHY_A_NEW_PROBE_WAS_UNAVOIDABLE_ring_IS_.the_new_probe: `collar` (tools/probes.py). EXPLICIT window holding ONE half, quoted in every output; subject = largest_component(luma > floor), the same subject rule as every other probe; 180 rays from the subject centroid; per ray the subject's own radius in that direction sets the scale; the RIDGE is the max of the luma profile in the FIXED radial window t in [0.35, 1.0] (the inner 35% is a constant geometric exclusion for the face-centre specular, not a fit). A ridge is 'a bright band out near the edge of this half' — the collar expressed as morphology. THERE IS NO COLOUR TEST ANYWHERE IN THE REGION OR THE RIDGE RULE, so the collar cannot escape it by changing hue, only by genuinely ceasing to be a bright band at that angle. I rendered the ridge points on both rounds and both plates and they trace the pale annulus. It reports sector ridge luma and max/min ('same brightness at every angle'), ridge width in px and its CV ('same width at every angle'), the ridge's radial position and CV, and pct_R_ge_255 over the ridge pixels so brightness cannot be bought back by clipping.
